lines: Crypto payments are final.
Pay the wrong seller, and your money is gone.
So people don't pay strangers.
This is Talaria.
Stripe for Portaldot, with a refund button.
Talaria prices trust.
Before a payment settles on Portaldot, we read the seller's reputation from Base.
A proven seller gets paid instantly.
A new seller's payment is held for thirty minutes, so the buyer can still dispute.
And every outcome is written back to Base, so reputation grows from what really happened.
Here's a real run, on testnet.
An AI agent buys from New Shop, a seller with no history.
The payment is held.
The buyer disputes, and the arbiter refunds in full.
The money goes back to Base, and New Shop gets negative feedback.
Then the same agent buys from Trusted Coffee, with a score of one hundred.
It settles instantly.
Checkout works from other chains.
This wallet has zero tPOT.
It locked test dollars on BNB testnet, the relayer credited it on Portaldot, and the invoice was paid without gas.
Base works the same way.
And merchants can refund from the payment page, in full or in part.
Agents get a budget, not your keys.
Our hosted agent has its own ERC-8004 identity, and its spending cap rises with its reputation.
Anyone can try it, with no wallet.
A signed mandate can limit it to one merchant and one amount.
Subscriptions, streams and remittance run on Base, and settle to Portaldot when you're ready.
It's all open source: a TypeScript SDK, an MCP server for agents, and docs.
Portaldot is the settlement hub.
Its V3 EVM runs standard Solidity, so value and reputation from other chains meet here.
Every step you saw has a transaction hash in our repo.
It's testnet only, with one trusted relayer and arbiter for now.
More attesters and mainnet come next.
Talaria.
Payments that can come back.
